sources.title: USDA FSIS — Food Thermometers
sources.what: A food thermometer is 'the only reliable way' to confirm safe minimum internal temperature; whole poultry checked in three places (innermost thigh, innermost wing, thickest breast), avoid bone; do not stuff whole poultry for optimum safety; stuffing centre must reach 165°F. Calibration section read in full 2026-11-20 (session f1fd0ff0): ice-water method — fill a glass with ice, add drinking water, stir, immerse the stem a minimum of 2 inches without touching the sides or bottom, wait a minimum of 30 seconds, the reading should be 32°F; boiling-water method — 2 inches deep, 30 seconds, 212°F at sea level, and boiling point falls by at least 2°F (possibly 5°F) at altitude. Care: wash by hand, most thermometers should not be immersed, and 'Do not leave your food thermometer in food while cooking unless the manufacturer's instructions specifically say it can withstand heat'. Type table: oven-cord, fork-combination and thermistor types are listed as 'Cannot be calibrated'; thermocouple can; most food thermometers read accurate within 2 to 4°F.
